gaps: B1 (blocker, contract-gap): the routing seam was not pinned — permission-classifier.ts only exposes eligibility and the named runtime directory is absent, so the refusal→ask branch was unspecified.

B2 (blocker, decision-conflict): AC3 made Allow-once reusable and promised scheduled-job benefit, conflicting with permission-decision-expiry.ts (immediate expiry), decisions 0040/0043 (once is never reusable) and 0121 (jobId-bearing decisions are pure functions of declared grants).

B3 (blocker, contract-gap): the mcp__gantry__file binding was unimplementable — it promised a literal capability id but named none, said list|read while excluding broad lists, artifactId reads and attachments (the motivating case).
G4 (gap, correctness): /dev/null was still admitted as a trusted-path candidate despite the stderr-redirect exception, and find needed adversarial argument tests.
G5 (gap, contract-gap): AC5 fail-closed and AC6 invariance were not scoped to interactive auto; a scheduled lane has no human listener and must keep deterministic denial plus card recovery.
contradictions: Fable UX lane: the spec kept 'attachment reads' fail-closed while the owner's complaint was specifically about reading an attachment they sent; and AC3 promised jobs stop re-asking while §1/0121 forbade the autonomous lane from consulting memory (resolved by rulings 1 and 2).
resolutions: R1 (owner): ALL attachments already in the conversation are readable with zero taps; bound to mcp__gantry__attachment_open (opaque ids, origin validated server-side at jobs/ipc-attachment-open-handler.ts:42-84) as birthright in interactive auto; mcp__gantry__file (actions list|read|write|promote_scratch) becomes argument-aware at gantry-tool-risk.ts:46-49 — resolves B3 and the first Fable contradiction.

R2 (owner): scheduled jobs DO consult learned decisions, projected as DECLARED GRANTS (deterministic lookup, updatedPermissions → autonomousAllowedToolRules; never the classifier) — decision 0153 drafted, amending 0121's 'never consults human-decision memory' clause; resolves B2's job half and the second Fable contradiction; AC5/AC6 scoped to interactive auto && !hostVerifiedJobId (hostJobId = permissionRunRestriction(...).jobId, ipc-permission-classifier-decision.ts:67-74) — resolves G5.

R3 (owner): tap semantics — [Allow] remembered (default, bold), [Just this once] NOT learned (today's allow_once path, 0040/0043 preserved), [No]; the human-decision store is a NEW record kind consulted before the classifier (writer today rejects human allow_once, permission-decision-memory-repository.postgres.ts:17-34) — resolves B2's allow_once half.

R4 (owner, dimension design delegated): generic scope — this exact action / this kind of action / this place — with a broadest-safe default (reads → kind anywhere; writes/destructive → exact), one 'Remembered: …' line and one narrower alternative; the scope store REUSES resolveTrustedRootStage (permission-decision-coordinator.ts:219-294), no second store; button labels change centrally (channels/permission-interaction.ts:74-88).

R5 (seam map, resolves B1): the classifier IS consulted; the force-ask is the classifier-allow VETO by a rail ASK signal (ipc-permission-classifier-decision.ts:307-308, 369-401). Change: carry railSignal from the rail callback (:111-119) and relax only that veto for interactive auto on out_of_trusted_root / read-only meta-executor signals; shared rails (domain/permission-deterministic-rails.ts:161-228) untouched.

R6 (owner + G4): workspace file writes judged by PATH; 2>/dev/null never a path candidate (permission-trusted-paths.ts pathCandidates ~:60); find read-only unless -delete/-exec/-execdir/-ok (bash-command-parser.ts:35,563,581) with adversarial tests; judge outage = one notice per conversation + deterministic reads still allow; /permissions view with Forget this; AC8 tap-budget fixtures replaying the 2026-09-02 log shapes.

rounds.chosen: Pick the best one which makes UX better

rounds.question: What should the default [Allow] remember when you don't pick a scope explicitly?

Writing files inside the workspace (FileWrite/Edit under the agent's own folders — the most common Claude-Code-auto action) is not mentioned by the spec today. Should it be judged by path (arg-aware: inside workspace = low, protected paths = ask) rather than by tool identity?

Two UX rules to confirm together: (a) a /permissions view that lists what was learned with 'Forget this'; (b) when the judge is down, one notice per conversation ('my safety judge is offline, I'll check with you more') and deterministic reads still allowed — not a tap storm.
